subtitle: Toasted noodle soup in tomato broth
verso: Golden fideo, never burnt: that's the lesson to be learnt.
story: The first soup most Mexican kids learn to love. Everything depends on toasting the noodles to the color of a peanut shell before the tomato goes in.

ingredients.title: Soup
items: 1 sprig cilantro (or a few leaves of epazote)

steps: Blend the tomatoes, onion and garlic with [[1 cup]] of the broth until smooth.
Heat the oil in a pot over medium. Add the fideo, breaking up the coils, and stir constantly until deep golden. Don't walk away; it burns fast.
Pour the tomato purée through a strainer into the pot. It will sizzle. Fry, stirring, 3 minutes until it darkens.
Add the rest of the broth, the salt and the cilantro. Simmer 8–10 minutes, until the fideo is soft.
Serve with lime, and crema and queso if you like.
pressureNote: No pressure-cooker version. This soup is done in 30 minutes on the stove, and the noodles would turn to mush.
tips: If the fideo browns too fast, pull the pot off the heat. It keeps cooking in the hot oil.

variations.name: Sopa Seca de Fideo
variations.subtitle: Dry fideo with chipotle
variations.note: A dry soup, cooked until the noodles absorb all the broth. It's the second course of a comida corrida: sopa aguada, then sopa seca, then the main stew.

items: Same as the base, but only 3 cups broth (1 for the purée, 2 to cook)
1–2 chipotles en adobo, blended with the tomato

steps: Toast the fideo and fry the tomato-chipotle purée as in the base.
Add [[2 cups]] broth, cover and cook on low 10 minutes until absorbed.
Top with crema, queso and avocado.
